You are reviewing PR #79 in the ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa repo (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront) as part of a senior engineer's PR review. This is a fresh, independent pass — do not assume any prior findings exist; report exactly what you find.

CONTEXT: This PR (branch fix/SFCC-856-csp-hardening-v2, base develop) implements nonce-based CSP for `style-src` to close a Lighthouse `csp-xss` finding. It touches exactly two files:
- overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts (Tier 1 — frozen, "wrong change = security hole on every page")
- overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx (Tier 2 — Global Shell, mounted on every page)

Get the live diff yourself: `gh pr diff 79` in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Also read the full current files at the PR head with `git show origin/fix/SFCC-856-csp-hardening-v2:overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` and `git show origin/fix/SFCC-856-csp-hardening-v2:overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`.

JIRA TICKET (SFCC-856) SUMMARY: "CSP hardening: nonce/hash-based script-src and style-src (csp-xss)". The ticket's description covers both `style-src`'s `'unsafe-inline'` AND `script-src`'s `'unsafe-eval'`/third-party wildcards as contributing to the failing `csp-xss` Lighthouse audit, and frames "thread the nonce through SSR rendering" as touching `overrides/app/ssr.js` (an absolutely-frozen file per AGENTS.md Hard Rule 4, no exception). The PR's actual implementation avoids touching ssr.js entirely (uses helmet's per-request directive-function support instead) and explicitly declares script-src's issues out of scope ("`'unsafe-eval'` is added by the MRT platform layer, not by this repo's own CSP config"; "third-party host allowlist... is a legitimate requirement... nonce-based CSP doesn't replace host allowlisting"). No ticket comments exist (verified — comment thread is empty).

WHAT HAS ALREADY BEEN INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — DO NOT RE-CHECK THESE, TAKE THEM AS GIVEN:
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` were run on both the PR head (25c8d3d) and base (develop @ a4f6921) in isolated worktrees. All four are byte-for-byte identical in output between head and base (same lint warnings/errors at the same lines, same 4 token-audit violations, same 408/408 real vitest passes across 26 files). This PR introduces zero new violations on any of these four gates. Do not re-run them.
- helmet@4.6.0 genuinely supports `(req, res) => string` CSP directive-value functions (confirmed against `node_modules/helmet/dist/middlewares/content-security-policy/*.d.ts`).
- `overrides/app/ssr.js` passes `contentSecurityPolicy` straight through to `helmet()` unmodified — confirmed by reading the file. No ssr.js change was needed or made.
- `@emotion/sheet` and `@emotion/react`'s SSR style-element path both genuinely read `cache.sheet.nonce` / `options.nonce` and attach a `nonce` attribute — confirmed by reading `node_modules/@emotion/sheet/dist/*.cjs.js` and `node_modules/@emotion/react/dist/*.cjs.js`. The nonce mechanism is real, not cargo-culted.
- The documented SHA256 hash `'sha256-GNF74DLkXb0fH3ILHgILFjk1ozCF3SNXQ5mQb7WLu/Y='` for Chakra's `preventTransition()` inline style was independently recomputed from the actual installed `@chakra-ui/color-mode@2.1.12` source (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/color-mode/dist/color-mode.utils.js`) and matches exactly.
- `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` already has a `react-helmet` module declaration (pre-existing) — no new type declaration was needed, confirmed.
- The `ChakraProvider` import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui` on line 8 of `_app-config/index.tsx` is unchanged context in the diff (pre-existing, not touched by this PR) — CodeRabbit initially flagged it then correctly retracted the finding for this reason.
- TimLavelleACC (PR author) is a genuine, verified member of the `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` GitHub team and holds repo admin — confirmed via `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members` and `gh api repos/.../collaborators/TimLavelleACC/permission`. The verified-session exception claimed in the PR body for touching the Tier 1 file is legitimate. CODEOWNERS correctly routes both changed files to the right approver teams.
- On the live MRT preview (https://zimmermann-pr-x856-39ca63c5.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com) the homepage renders with full Chakra styling intact and zero CSP violation messages in the browser console. A response header dump confirmed the live CSP header genuinely contains the split `style-src`/`style-src-elem`/`style-src-attr` directives with a real per-request nonce value and the hash.

YOUR JOB — look for anything NOT already covered above. In particular:
1. Read both files end-to-end for correctness bugs: null/undefined handling, hydration-mismatch risk between server and client render output, memoization correctness (`useMemo(() => createCache({key:'css', nonce: cspNonce}), [cspNonce])` and `getOrCreateNonce`'s `res.locals` memoization), TypeScript soundness of the `ResponseWithLocals` cast.
2. Security review specific to the nonce mechanism: is `randomBytes(16)` sufficient entropy (128 bits)? Any way the nonce or its cache key could leak, collide, or be predictable? Does the `<meta name="csp-nonce">` handoff from server to client create any XSS or nonce-disclosure risk beyond what's inherent to the nonce pattern itself? Does splitting `style-src-attr` back to plain `'unsafe-inline'` (no nonce) meaningfully reopen any part of the original `csp-xss` finding, or is that a correct, narrow, unavoidable carve-out?
3. Whether this PR's `_app-config/index.tsx` changes could affect any OTHER consumer of `AppConfig`/`ChakraProvider` not visible in this two-file diff — e.g., check `.storybook/preview.tsx` (read-only, it's Tier 1 test config, don't suggest edits) for whether Storybook's own Chakra/emotion mounting now diverges from the app's in any way that matters, and check whether any other file in `overrides/` imports `_app-config` directly and might assume the old (non-CacheProvider-wrapped) tree shape.
4. Whether the PR's framing that `script-src`'s issues are "not fixable from this repo" is actually correct, or whether there's a legitimate way this repo could still improve `script-src` that the PR is prematurely ruling out (e.g., check whether `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/middleware` — imported and applied in `ssr.js` before the custom `helmet()` call — itself sets a `script-src`/CSP header that composes or conflicts with the custom one, since that would be directly checkable from `node_modules`).
5. Anything else that reads as a genuine correctness, security, or regression risk — but do not flag pre-existing/inherited issues as new, and do not flag style/convention nitpicks (a separate reviewer is covering those).

Report back a plain list of findings. For each: what you found, the file:line, why it matters (concrete failure scenario), and how confident you are (did you confirm it by reading actual source, or is it a suspicion that would need more digging). If you find nothing beyond what's already covered above, say so plainly — that is a useful, valid result, not a failure to find something.

content.text:
Investigation complete. I read both changed files at the PR head, the diff, `ssr.js`, and then went deep into `node_modules` (helmet, express, `@emotion/react`/`cache`, `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`, and the actual installed `lighthouse`/`csp_evaluator` packages) plus live-tested the PR's own MRT preview with repeated `curl` requests. Two of the findings below are substantive and not covered by the pre-verified list; the rest are smaller confirmations from the five specific angles requested.

## Findings

**1. CDN caching defeats the nonce's per-request uniqueness on the site's two highest-traffic page types — HIGH confidence, empirically verified live.**
`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:117-118` and `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:180` both call `res.set('Cache-Control', 's-maxage=..., stale-while-revalidate=...')` (pre-existing, not touched by this PR). I curled the PR's live preview 5 times in a row:
```
x-cache: Hit from cloudfront   (all 5 requests)
cache-control: s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=900
age: 60, 62, 63, 64, 65        (climbing — same cached object)
style-src-elem ... 'nonce-Qh5r+26oiEGz+ogUaJVySQ==' ...   (identical on all 5 hits)
```
`getOrCreateNonce` in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts:38-46` does generate a fresh, cryptographically random nonce per *origin* request — that part is correct. But once CloudFront caches that response for 900s (confirmed live), the exact same nonce is replayed to every visitor of that cached page for the full cache lifetime. A nonce's entire security value rests on being unpredictable *before* the response exists; here, anyone (including an attacker) can read the current nonce off any normal page load and reuse it for the whole cache window. This doesn't break rendering or produce console errors — it silently downgrades the nonce, for homepage/PDP specifically, to roughly the strength of a static allowlist for up to 15 minutes at a time. Neither the PR nor the ticket mentions this interaction. It isn't fixable inside the two changed files — the standard fix (edge-compute nonce rewrite on cache HIT, e.g. a CloudFront Function) lives outside `overrides/` entirely, and the alternative (stop caching HTML) conflicts with this project's stated mobile-perf priority. Worth a conscious team decision, not a blocker on its own — it's still strictly better than the pre-PR always-open `'unsafe-inline'` for anything uncached.

**2. Lighthouse's `csp-xss` audit never evaluates `style-src` at all — this PR cannot move the metric the ticket names, verified against this repo's own installed packages.**
Traced `node_modules/lighthouse/lighthouse-core/audits/csp-xss.js` → `node_modules/csp_evaluator/lighthouse/lighthouse_checks.ts`'s `evaluateForFailure()` (the sole function whose output determines the audit's score: `score = bypasses.length ? 0 : 1`). It runs exactly: `checkMissingScriptSrcDirective`, `checkMissingObjectSrcDirective`, `checkMultipleMissingBaseUriDirective`, `checkStrictDynamic`, `checkScriptUnsafeInline`, `checkWildcards`, `checkPlainUrlSchemes`. Every one of these is hardcoded to `script-src`/`object-src`/`base-uri` — the last two via `DIRECTIVES_CAUSING_XSS = [SCRIPT_SRC, OBJECT_SRC, BASE_URI]` in `csp_evaluator/checks/security_checks.ts:33-34`. `style-src`/`style-src-elem`/`style-src-attr` appear in none of these checks and nowhere in the finding-to-message map either. Applying this to the actual live header I captured, the specific, current trigger is very likely `checkStrictDynamic`: this app's `script-src` is a plain host allowlist (`storage.googleapis.com`, `*.stripe.com`, etc.) with no `'strict-dynamic'`, which that checker treats as a score-zeroing finding — not `'unsafe-eval'` (there's no dedicated unsafe-eval check in this audit) and not style-src. Practical upshot: the Jira ticket's premise that style-src's `'unsafe-inline'` contributes to the failing `csp-xss` audit appears to be factually wrong for this specific Lighthouse check, so this PR — however well-built — will not close that finding; only the script-src work the PR declares out of scope can. (Separately confirmed: this repo's own `lighthouserc.js` uses the `lighthouse:recommended` preset, which per `node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/presets/recommended.js` doesn't assert on `csp-xss` individually anyway, so this isn't currently a CI-blocking gate either way — it's presumably tracked from a manual/external Lighthouse run.) The style-src work remains a legitimate, independent hardening improvement on its own merits; it just isn't the fix for the audit named in the ticket.

**3. `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` forcibly re-merges `'unsafe-eval'` + wildcard hosts into `script-src` on every response — confirms the PR's "not fixable from this repo" framing, with a sharper mechanism than the PR itself states.**
`overrides/app/ssr.js` runs `app.use(defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders)` before `app.use(helmet({contentSecurityPolicy}))`. That function (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/middleware/security.js:25-77`) monkey-patches `res.setHeader` so that *any* later call setting the CSP header — including helmet's own — gets union-merged with a required set containing `'script-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-eval'", runtimeAdmin, '*.site.com']`. So even if `contentSecurityPolicy.ts`'s own script-src array never mentioned `'unsafe-eval'`, the final response would still carry it; the only way to stop that is to stop calling this middleware in `ssr.js`, which is absolutely frozen (Hard Rule 4, no exception). Bonus finding: this repo's own script-src array doesn't include `'self'` at all — the app's own bundle scripts structurally depend on this merge just to load. Confirmed this merge's required-directive set has no `style-src*` entries, so it has zero interaction with this PR's actual changes. Forward-looking note for whoever scopes script-src next: a future nonce/`strict-dynamic` script-src would get the same forced re-merge, undermining much of its value unless addressed — not a defect in this PR, just context worth having going in.

**4–10, confirmatory checks (no defect found; reported since they were explicitly asked about):**
- **TypeScript soundness of `ResponseWithLocals` cast** (`contentSecurityPolicy.ts:41`): sound. `node_modules/express/lib/middleware/init.js:38` (`res.locals = res.locals || Object.create(null)`) guarantees `res.locals` is a real object on every request before any user middleware runs.
- **Memoization / per-request cache** (`_app-config/index.tsx:164`): correct, and better than a hypothetical shared default cache — creating a fresh `createCache()` per request (since `cspNonce` differs per request) is Emotion's own documented SSR pattern and avoids the classic "shared cache mutated across requests" SSR footgun.
- **Ordering/race check**: `node_modules/helmet/dist/middlewares/content-security-policy/index.js` evaluates directive functions and calls `res.setHeader` synchronously inside its own `app.use` middleware, which runs before `app.get('*', runtime.render)` later in the chain — so `res.locals.cspNonce` is always populated before `AppConfig` renders. No race.
- **Storybook divergence** (`.storybook/preview.tsx`): mounts `ChakraProvider` with no `CacheProvider`/nonce. Confirmed immaterial — Storybook doesn't enforce the app's CSP header. Confirmed no other file in `overrides/` imports `_app-config` directly (all other grep hits are comments referencing it by name), so nothing else assumes the old tree shape.
- **`style-src-attr: 'unsafe-inline'` carve-out**: confirmed narrow and currently risk-free in this codebase specifically — `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` (the only rich-text/CMS renderer touching `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`-adjacent territory) explicitly discards every HTML attribute when converting SFCC copy to React elements, so CMS content can never produce a live inline `style=` attribute. The only real `style={{...}}` usages in the codebase are static developer literals (`zimmLogo`, and an unrelated scaffold page).
- **`@emotion/cache` phantom dependency**: not declared in `package.json` (neither is `@emotion/react`, which is already imported the same way pre-existing this PR in `theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx`/`theme/fontFace.tsx`). Low risk — `@emotion/cache` is a hard dependency of `@emotion/react` per `package-lock.json`, so it's guaranteed present wherever `@emotion/react` already resolves; this PR just extends an already-accepted pattern.
- **No `res.locals.cspNonce` collision**: grepped `overrides/app/ssr/{paymentMetadata,marketingCloud,slasTokens}.ts` on the PR branch — none read or write that key.

No other correctness, hydration, or regression risks turned up beyond the above and what was already given as pre-verified.
